newsitem.title: USA: US FDA proposes timeframe on food health claims.
newsitem.headline: US FDA proposes timeframe on food health claims.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Monday proposed establishing a timeframe for new regulations on health claims for foods and dietary supplements.

The agency said that within 270 days of the date of publication of proposed regulations, it would publish a final rule that either authorizes use of a health claim or explains why it was not okayed. FDA would be able to extend the period.
In a notice in the Federal Register, FDA said the timetable was prompted by a recent court decision. It said written comments on the proposed timetable must be received by April 16.
